```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)
library(factoextra)
library(knitr)
library(DT)
library(tidyr)
library(mixOmics)
library(pls)

# Set up tutorial options
tutorial_options(exercise.timelimit = 60)

# Note: In practice, students would load their own data
# For this tutorial, we'll create a simulated dataset with similar structure
# In real use: metabolomics_data <- readxl::read_excel("metabolomics.xlsx", sheet = 1)

# Simulate metabolomics data structure (57 observations, 655 NMR variables)
set.seed(42)
n_samples <- 57
n_vars <- 655

# Create sample IDs based on the description
# MYB76: A1-A8, B1-B8, C1-C8 (Class 1)
# Wild type: D1-D8, E1-E8, F1-F8 (Class 0)
sample_ids <- c(
  paste0("A", 1:8), paste0("B", 1:8), paste0("C", 1:8),  # MYB76
  paste0("D", 1:8), paste0("E", 1:8), paste0("F", 1:7)   # Wild type (46 samples + replicates)
)

# Add some analytical replicates
sample_ids <- c(sample_ids, paste0(sample(sample_ids, 11), "_rep"))
sample_ids <- sample_ids[1:n_samples]

# Create class labels
class_labels <- ifelse(substr(sample_ids, 1, 1) %in% c("A", "B", "C"), 1, 0)

# Extract tree and internode information
tree_letter <- substr(sample_ids, 1, 1)
internode <- as.numeric(gsub("[A-F]|_rep", "", sample_ids))
internode[is.na(internode)] <- sample(1:8, sum(is.na(internode)), replace = TRUE)

# Simulate NMR data with realistic structure
# Create base profiles for each class
metabolomics_data <- data.frame(
  Sample_ID = sample_ids,
  Class = factor(class_labels, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Wild_Type", "MYB76")),
  Tree = tree_letter,
  Internode = internode
)

# Generate NMR variables (chemical shift regions)
# Add class-specific patterns and internode trends
for(i in 1:n_vars) {
  # Base signal
  signal <- rnorm(n_samples, mean = 5, sd = 2)
  
  # Add class effect (some variables differentiate classes)
  if(i <= 200) {  # First 200 variables have class differences
    signal <- signal + ifelse(class_labels == 1, rnorm(n_samples, 2, 0.5), rnorm(n_samples, -2, 0.5))
  }
  
  # Add internode trend (growth effect)
  if(i > 200 && i <= 400) {
    signal <- signal + internode * 0.3 + rnorm(n_samples, 0, 0.5)
  }
  
  # Add tree-specific variation
  signal <- signal + rnorm(n_samples, 0, 0.3)
  
  # Ensure positive values (like NMR intensities)
  signal <- abs(signal)
  
  # Create variable name (chemical shift region)
  var_name <- sprintf("NMR_%.2f", 0.02 * i)
  metabolomics_data[[var_name]] <- signal
}

# Store variable names
nmr_vars <- grep("NMR_", names(metabolomics_data), value = TRUE)
```

## Background

A gene encoding MYB transcription factor, with unknown function, **PttMYB76**, was selected from a library of poplar trees for metabolomic characterization of the growth process in Poplar trees.

### The Biological Question

The PttMYB76 gene is believed to affect different pathways in the phenyl propanoid synthetic pathway. This pathway leads to the formation of:
- S- and G-lignin
- Flavonoids  
- Sinapate esters

### Experimental Design

![Poplar Plant Sampling Design](https://via.placeholder.com/300x400.png?text=Poplar+Tree+Internodes+1-8+from+top+to+bottom)

**Figure**: Poplar plant response vector (internodes). The growth- or time-related response vector, where internode 1 is at the top (youngest) and internode 8 at the bottom (oldest).

**Sample Collection:**
- 12-week-old poplar plants
- Two genotypes:
  - **Wild Type (WT)**: Trees D, E, F (Class 0)
  - **MYB76 modified**: Trees A, B, C (Class 1)
- 3 trees per genotype
- 8 internodes per tree (apex removed before sampling)
- Total: 46 plant samples + analytical replicates = 57 observations

### Data Structure

- **N = 57 observations**: 6 trees × 8 internodes + replicates
- **K = 655 variables**: ¹H-NMR chemical shift regions (0.02 ppm buckets)
- **Response variable**: Class (0 = Wild Type, 1 = MYB76)
- **Growth vector**: Internode number (1 = top/young, 8 = bottom/old)

```{r explore-data, exercise=TRUE}
# Examine the data structure
head(metabolomics_data[, 1:10])  # First few columns

# Check dimensions
cat("Number of samples:", nrow(metabolomics_data), "\n")
cat("Number of variables:", length(nmr_vars), "\n")

# Class distribution
table(metabolomics_data$Class)

# Tree distribution
table(metabolomics_data$Tree)
```

2. **Identify differences and putative biomarkers** using:

4. **Describe model diagnostics** of PLS-DA models

## Understanding Scaling Methods

Before we start, let's understand different scaling approaches:

```{r scaling-info, echo=FALSE}
cat("SCALING METHODS IN METABOLOMICS:\n\n")

cat("1. NO SCALING (Mean-centered only):\n")
cat("   - Variables keep their original variance\n")
cat("   - High-intensity signals dominate the model\n")
cat("   - Use when: All variables have similar ranges\n\n")

cat("2. UNIT VARIANCE (UV) SCALING:\n")
cat("   - Divide by standard deviation\n")
cat("   - All variables have equal importance\n")
cat("   - Use when: You want to emphasize small peaks equally\n")
cat("   - Analysis based on correlations, not covariances\n\n")

cat("3. PARETO SCALING:\n")
cat("   - Divide by square root of standard deviation\n")
cat("   - Intermediate between No scaling and UV\n")
cat("   - Large variances reduced more than small ones\n")
cat("   - Preferred for metabolomics: balances signal importance\n\n")
```

### Visualizing Scaling Effects

```{r scaling-demo, exercise=TRUE}
# Take a few example variables to demonstrate scaling
example_vars <- metabolomics_data[, c("NMR_1.00", "NMR_5.00", "NMR_10.00")]

# Function to apply different scaling
apply_scaling <- function(x, method = "none") {
  x_centered <- scale(x, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
  
  if(method == "uv") {
    return(scale(x, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE))
  } else if(method == "pareto") {
    sds <- apply(x, 2, sd)
    return(scale(x, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) / sqrt(sds))
  } else {
    return(x_centered)
  }
}

# Compare standard deviations
cat("Standard deviations before scaling:\n")
print(apply(example_vars, 2, sd))

cat("\nStandard deviations after UV scaling:\n")
print(apply(apply_scaling(example_vars, "uv"), 2, sd))

cat("\nStandard deviations after Pareto scaling:\n")
print(apply(apply_scaling(example_vars, "pareto"), 2, sd))
```

## PCA Analysis with Pareto Scaling

Let's start with an unsupervised PCA using Pareto scaling:

```{r pca-pareto, exercise=TRUE}
# Extract NMR variables
X <- metabolomics_data[, nmr_vars]

# Apply Pareto scaling
X_centered <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
sds <- apply(X, 2, sd)
X_pareto <- X_centered / sqrt(sds)

# Perform PCA
pca_result <- prcomp(X_pareto, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)

# Summary
summary(pca_result)

# Calculate variance explained
variance_explained <- pca_result$sdev^2
total_variance <- sum(variance_explained)
r2_values <- variance_explained / total_variance
r2_cumulative <- cumsum(r2_values)

cat("\nVariance explained by first 5 PCs:\n")
for(i in 1:5) {
  cat(sprintf("PC%d: %.1f%%\n", i, r2_values[i]*100))
}
cat(sprintf("\nCumulative (PC1-PC2): %.1f%%\n", r2_cumulative[2]*100))
cat(sprintf("Cumulative (PC1-PC3): %.1f%%\n", r2_cumulative[3]*100))
```

```{r pca-pareto-solution}
X <- metabolomics_data[, nmr_vars]
X_centered <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
sds <- apply(X, 2, sd)
X_pareto <- X_centered / sqrt(sds)
pca_result <- prcomp(X_pareto, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
summary(pca_result)
```

### Quiz: PCA Quality Assessment

```{r quiz-pca-quality}
quiz(
  question("How many components did the PCA calculate and what does this tell you about the data?",
    answer("It calculated 57 components (number of samples)"),
    answer("It calculated components up to min(n-1, p)", correct = TRUE),
    answer("It only calculated 2 components"),
    answer("It calculated 655 components"),
    message = "PCA can calculate at most min(n-1, p) components. With 57 samples, we can get up to 56 components."
  ),
  question("What does it mean if some samples have high leverage or are outliers?",
    answer("They are measurement errors and should always be removed"),
    answer("They may represent unique biological variation", correct = TRUE),
    answer("The PCA model is invalid"),
    answer("The scaling was wrong"),
    message = "Outliers in metabolomics can indicate biological variation, sample degradation, or analytical issues. They need investigation, not automatic removal."
  )
)
```

```{r pca-scores, exercise=TRUE}
# Create scores dataframe
scores_df <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_result$x[,1],
  PC2 = pca_result$x[,2],
  PC3 = pca_result$x[,3],
  Sample_ID = metabolomics_data$Sample_ID,
  Class = metabolomics_data$Class,
  Tree = metabolomics_data$Tree,
  Internode = metabolomics_data$Internode
)

# Scores plot colored by Class
p1 <- ggplot(scores_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Class, shape = Class)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "PCA Scores Plot - Colored by Class",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(r2_values[1]*100, 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(r2_values[2]*100, 1), "%)")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Wild_Type" = "#0072B2", "MYB76" = "#D55E00")) +

```

## Variable Importance in PLS-DA

Identifying the most important variables (potential biomarkers):

```{r plsda-vip, exercise=TRUE}
# Calculate VIP (Variable Importance in Projection) scores
# VIP > 1 indicates important variables

# Function to calculate VIP
vip_scores <- function(model) {
  # Get loadings and explained variance
  W <- model$loading.weights
  Q <- model$Yloadings
  
  # Calculate VIP for each variable
  SS <- colSums(Q^2) * colSums(model$scores^2)
  Wnorm2 <- colSums(W^2)
  SSW <- sweep(W^2, 2, SS, "*")
  
  vip <- sqrt(nrow(SSW) * apply(SSW, 1, sum) / sum(SS))
  return(vip)
}

vip <- vip_scores(plsda_model)

# Get top 30 VIP scores
top_vip_idx <- order(vip, decreasing = TRUE)[1:30]
top_vip_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(vip)[top_vip_idx],
  VIP = vip[top_vip_idx]
)

# Plot VIP scores
ggplot(top_vip_df, aes(x = reorder(Variable, VIP), y = VIP)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 30 Variables by VIP Score",
       subtitle = "VIP > 1 indicates important variables",
       x = "NMR Variable", y = "VIP Score") +
  theme_minimal()

cat("\nVariables with VIP > 1:\n")
important_vars <- names(vip)[vip > 1]
cat(length(important_vars), "variables\n")
```

### Loadings Plot for PLS-DA

```{r plsda-loadings, exercise=TRUE}
# Extract loadings
loadings <- loadings(plsda_model)[,1:2]

# Plot only top variables by VIP
top_vars <- names(vip)[order(vip, decreasing = TRUE)[1:50]]
loadings_subset <- loadings[top_vars, ]

loadings_plot_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(loadings_subset),
  LV1 = loadings_subset[,1],
  LV2 = loadings_subset[,2],
  VIP = vip[top_vars]
)

ggplot(loadings_plot_df, aes(x = LV1, y = LV2, size = VIP)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "PLS-DA Loadings Plot (Top 50 by VIP)",
       x = "LV1 Loadings", y = "LV2 Loadings",
       size = "VIP Score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Model Diagnostics and Validation

### Permutation Testing

```{r permutation-test, exercise=TRUE}
# Perform permutation test to assess model significance
set.seed(123)
n_perms <- 100

# Original Q2
original_Q2 <- Q2[optimal_ncomp]

# Permutation Q2 values
perm_Q2 <- numeric(n_perms)

for(i in 1:n_perms) {
  # Permute class labels
  Y_perm <- sample(Y)
  
  # Fit model
  perm_model <- plsr(Y_perm ~ X_pareto, ncomp = optimal_ncomp, validation = "LOO")
  
  # Calculate Q2
  PRESS_perm <- perm_model$validation$PRESS[optimal_ncomp + 1]
  TSS_perm <- sum((Y_perm - mean(Y_perm))^2)
  perm_Q2[i] <- 1 - PRESS_perm / TSS_perm
}

# Plot permutation distribution
hist(perm_Q2, breaks = 20, col = "lightblue", 
     main = "Permutation Test - Q2 Distribution",
     xlab = "Q2 Value", xlim = c(min(perm_Q2, original_Q2), max(perm_Q2, original_Q2)))
abline(v = original_Q2, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Original Q2"), col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

# P-value
p_value <- sum(perm_Q2 >= original_Q2) / n_perms
cat(sprintf("\nOriginal Q2: %.3f\n", original_Q2))
cat(sprintf("P-value: %.3f\n", p_value))
cat(sprintf("Interpretation: %s\n", 
            ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "Model is significant!", "Model may not be significant.")))
```

### Cross-Validation Predictions

```{r cv-predictions, exercise=TRUE}
# Examine cross-validation predictions
cv_preds <- plsda_model$validation$pred[,,optimal_ncomp]
cv_class <- ifelse(cv_preds > 0.5, "MYB76", "Wild_Type")

# CV Confusion matrix
cv_confusion <- table(Predicted = cv_class, True = metabolomics_data$Class)
print("Cross-Validation Confusion Matrix:")
print(cv_confusion)

# CV Accuracy
cv_accuracy <- sum(diag(cv_confusion)) / sum(cv_confusion)
cat(sprintf("\nCross-Validation Accuracy: %.1f%%\n", cv_accuracy * 100))

# Compare to training accuracy
cat(sprintf("Training Accuracy: %.1f%%\n", accuracy * 100))
cat(sprintf("Difference: %.1f%%\n", (accuracy - cv_accuracy) * 100))

if(accuracy - cv_accuracy > 0.1) {
  cat("\nWarning: Large difference suggests potential overfitting!\n")
} else {
  cat("\nGood: Training and CV accuracies are similar.\n")
}
```

### Practice Exercise

```{r final-exercise, exercise=TRUE}
# Complete analysis workflow:
# 1. Load and scale data
# 2. Perform PCA
# 3. Perform PLS-DA
# 4. Identify top biomarkers
# 5. Validate the model

# Your code here:


```

```{r final-exercise-solution}
# Complete workflow
# 1. Prepare data
X <- as.matrix(metabolomics_data[, nmr_vars])
Y <- as.numeric(metabolomics_data$Class) - 1
X_centered <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
sds <- apply(X, 2, sd)
X_pareto <- X_centered / sqrt(sds)

# 2. PCA
pca_final <- prcomp(X_pareto, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
cat("PCA variance explained (PC1-PC2):", 
    round(sum(pca_final$sdev[1:2]^2) / sum(pca_final$sdev^2) * 100, 1), "%\n")

# 3. PLS-DA
plsda_final <- plsr(Y ~ X_pareto, ncomp = 3, validation = "LOO")

# 4. Calculate Q2
PRESS <- plsda_final$validation$PRESS
TSS <- sum((Y - mean(Y))^2)
Q2_final <- 1 - PRESS / TSS
cat("\nQ2 values:", round(Q2_final, 3), "\n")

# 5. Get predictions and accuracy
preds <- predict(plsda_final, ncomp = 2)
pred_class <- ifelse(preds > 0.5, 1, 0)
accuracy_final <- mean(pred_class == Y)
cat("Accuracy:", round(accuracy_final * 100, 1), "%\n")
```

### Next Steps in Real Research

1. **Metabolite Identification**: Use 2D-NMR and MS to identify specific compounds
2. **Pathway Analysis**: Map biomarkers to metabolic pathways
3. **Independent Validation**: Test in new samples
4. **Quantification**: Develop targeted methods for key biomarkers
5. **Integration**: Combine with genomics/transcriptomics data
6. **Biological Follow-up**: Functional studies of identified pathways

### Key Differences: PCA vs PLS-DA

**When to use PCA:**
- Exploratory data analysis
- No prior knowledge of groups
- Identify overall patterns and outliers
- Understand main sources of variation

**When to use PLS-DA:**
- Known groups to classify
- Find discriminating biomarkers
- Build predictive models
- After PCA exploration
- **Always validate with cross-validation!**

  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p2)

## PCA-Class Models

PCA-Class performs separate PCA models for each class to examine within-class variation:

```{r pca-class, exercise=TRUE}
# Split data by class
myb76_data <- metabolomics_data[metabolomics_data$Class == "MYB76", nmr_vars]
wt_data <- metabolomics_data[metabolomics_data$Class == "Wild_Type", nmr_vars]

# Apply Pareto scaling to each class separately
myb76_centered <- scale(myb76_data, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
myb76_sds <- apply(myb76_data, 2, sd)
myb76_pareto <- myb76_centered / sqrt(myb76_sds)

wt_centered <- scale(wt_data, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
wt_sds <- apply(wt_data, 2, sd)
wt_pareto <- wt_centered / sqrt(wt_sds)

# PCA for each class
pca_myb76 <- prcomp(myb76_pareto, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
pca_wt <- prcomp(wt_pareto, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)

# Summaries
cat("MYB76 Class PCA:\n")
summary(pca_myb76)

cat("\n\nWild Type Class PCA:\n")
summary(pca_wt)
```

## PLS-DA (Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis)

PLS-DA is a supervised method that finds components maximizing the covariance between X (NMR data) and Y (class labels):

```{r plsda-model, exercise=TRUE}
# Prepare data for PLS-DA
X <- as.matrix(metabolomics_data[, nmr_vars])
Y <- as.numeric(metabolomics_data$Class) - 1  # Convert to 0/1

# Apply Pareto scaling
X_centered <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
sds <- apply(X, 2, sd)
X_pareto <- X_centered / sqrt(sds)

# Fit PLS-DA model using plsr from pls package
# Start with 5 components, will optimize later
plsda_model <- plsr(Y ~ X_pareto, ncomp = 5, validation = "LOO")

# Summary
summary(plsda_model)

# Calculate R2 and Q2 equivalents
R2 <- R2(plsda_model)
RMSEP_values <- RMSEP(plsda_model, estimate = "CV")

cat("\nModel Quality Metrics:\n")
print(R2)
```

```{r plsda-model-solution}
X <- as.matrix(metabolomics_data[, nmr_vars])
Y <- as.numeric(metabolomics_data$Class) - 1
X_centered <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
sds <- apply(X, 2, sd)
X_pareto <- X_centered / sqrt(sds)
plsda_model <- plsr(Y ~ X_pareto, ncomp = 5, validation = "LOO")
summary(plsda_model)
```

### Determine Optimal Components

```{r plsda-components, exercise=TRUE}
# Plot validation results to determine optimal components
plot(RMSEP(plsda_model), legendpos = "topright",
     main = "RMSEP for PLS-DA Model")

# Calculate Q2 (predictive ability)
# Q2 is based on cross-validation
PRESS <- plsda_model$validation$PRESS
TSS <- sum((Y - mean(Y))^2)
Q2 <- 1 - PRESS / TSS

cat("\nQ2 values by component:\n")
print(Q2)

# Typically select components where Q2 > 0.5 and stops improving
optimal_ncomp <- which(Q2 > 0.5)[1]
if(is.na(optimal_ncomp)) optimal_ncomp <- 2

cat(sprintf("\nSuggested optimal components: %d\n", optimal_ncomp))
```

### Quiz: PLS-DA Model Quality

```{r quiz-plsda-quality}
quiz(
  question("How many components did the PLS-DA model use and why is this important?",
    answer("Always use all components"),
    answer("Use components with Q2 > 0.5", correct = TRUE),
    answer("Always use exactly 2 components"),
    answer("Use as many as possible"),
    message = "Components should be selected based on cross-validation (Q2). Stop when Q2 decreases or becomes negative (overfitting)."
  ),
  question("What does Q2 represent in a PLS-DA model?",
    answer("The percentage of variance explained"),
    answer("The predictive ability based on cross-validation", correct = TRUE),
    answer("The number of samples"),
    answer("The correlation between variables"),
    message = "Q2 indicates how well the model predicts new samples. Q2 > 0.5 is generally considered good for metabolomics."
  ),
  question("How much do you trust this PLS-DA model?",
    answer("Complete trust - it's perfect"),
    answer("Good trust if Q2 > 0.5 and validated", correct = TRUE),
    answer("No trust - supervised methods always overfit"),
    answer("Trust only R2 values"),
    message = "Trust depends on cross-validation results (Q2), separation in scores plots, and biological validation. Q2 > 0.5 with good separation is encouraging."
  )
)
```

## PLS-DA Scores and Predictions

```{r plsda-scores, exercise=TRUE}
# Extract PLS-DA scores
plsda_scores <- scores(plsda_model)[,1:2]  # First 2 components

# Create scores dataframe
plsda_scores_df <- data.frame(
  LV1 = plsda_scores[,1],
  LV2 = plsda_scores[,2],
  Class = metabolomics_data$Class,
  Sample_ID = metabolomics_data$Sample_ID,
  Internode = metabolomics_data$Internode,
  Tree = metabolomics_data$Tree
)

# PLS-DA scores plot
ggplot(plsda_scores_df, aes(x = LV1, y = LV2, color = Class, shape = Class)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "PLS-DA Scores Plot",
       x = "Latent Variable 1",
       y = "Latent Variable 2") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Wild_Type" = "#0072B2", "MYB76" = "#D55E00")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r plsda-predictions, exercise=TRUE}
# Get predictions
predictions <- predict(plsda_model, ncomp = optimal_ncomp)
predicted_class <- ifelse(predictions > 0.5, "MYB76", "Wild_Type")
true_class <- metabolomics_data$Class

# Confusion matrix
confusion_matrix <- table(Predicted = predicted_class, True = true_class)
print(confusion_matrix)

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy <- sum(diag(confusion_matrix)) / sum(confusion_matrix)
cat(sprintf("\nClassification Accuracy: %.1f%%\n", accuracy * 100))

# Sensitivity and Specificity
sensitivity <- confusion_matrix["MYB76", "MYB76"] / sum(confusion_matrix[, "MYB76"])
specificity <- confusion_matrix["Wild_Type", "Wild_Type"] / sum(confusion_matrix[, "Wild_Type"])

cat(sprintf("Sensitivity (MYB76): %.1f%%\n", sensitivity * 100))
cat(sprintf("Specificity (Wild Type): %.1f%%\n", specificity * 100))
```
